punchline: Enron asked the SEC for the right to book a contract's whole future profit on the day it was signed.
thirty_sec: In 1991 Enron's new gas trading unit asked the SEC for permission to use mark-to-market accounting: book all of a contract's future profit the day it is signed. After months of letters and two meetings, the staff sent a no-objection letter in January 1992. A Senate committee later concluded Enron had at minimum overestimated the values it marked, because long contracts have no market price to check against.
